facts.value: See the per-benefit keys fed.bik.*.conditions; employment-tax treatment per benefit is in fed.base.* (Pub. 15-B (2026) Table 2-1 p.6).

Qualified individual covered by a high deductible health plan and by no other health coverage except permitted coverage; 2026 HDHP: deductible at least 1,700 self-only / 3,400 family, out-of-pocket max 8,500 / 17,000; no contributions after Medicare enrolment; employer contributions comparable for comparable coverage (35% excise otherwise) unless made through a cafeteria plan, where cafeteria nondiscrimination rules apply; partners and 2% S-corporation shareholders cannot make pre-tax contributions; report in W-2 box 12 code W.

Offered only through a section 125 cafeteria plan; salary reduction for plan years beginning in 2026 capped at 3,400 (a plan without the cap is not a cafeteria plan); optional carryover instead of a grace period.

Written dependent care assistance program for employees only; services for a qualifying person and needed to let the employee work; exclusion up to 7,500 (3,750 married filing separately) and not above the smaller of the employee's or spouse's earned income; not for highly compensated employees unless the program is nondiscriminatory (section 129(d)).

Separate written educational assistance program for employees only; nondiscriminatory in favour of highly compensated employees; not more than 5% of benefits to more-than-5% owners; no choice of cash instead; covers tuition, fees, books, supplies, equipment and qualified student-loan payments; exclusion up to 5,250 a year.
facts.note: Pub. 15-B (2026) Educational Assistance, p.11; Table 2-1 p.6.

facts.value: Commuter highway vehicle and transit passes up to 340 a month and qualified parking up to 340 a month are excluded; not available to 2% S-corporation shareholders; cannot be offered through a cafeteria plan.
facts.note: Pub. 15-B (2026) Table 2-1 p.6 and p.4 (benefits not allowed in a cafeteria plan).

facts.value: From 2026-07-04 the employer may contribute up to 2,500 a year toward the 5,000 Trump account limit of an employee or dependent, excluded from gross income if paid under a separate written plan for the exclusive benefit of employees meeting requirements similar to section 129(d)(2), (3), (6), (7) and (8).
facts.note: Pub. 15-A (2026) What's New and sec. 5 Employer Contributions to Trump Accounts (local HTML). FICA/FUTA treatment not stated: see unresolved fed.bik.trump_account.employment_tax_treatment. NOTE (proposed rule only): section 128 proposed regulations (IRB 2026-37, 2026-09-08) state that excludable employer contributions remain FICA/FUTA wages with no income-tax withholding; NOT final; level employer withholding/reporting [US-FEDV6-042]. Do not configure as a rule.

facts.value: Fair market value: the amount an employee would have to pay a third party in an arm's-length transaction to buy or lease the benefit, on all facts and circumstances; neither the employee's view of the value nor the employer's cost determines it.
facts.note: Pub. 15-B (2026) section 3, General Valuation Rule, p.26.

facts.value: Include in pay the amount by which the value of the benefit exceeds the sum of any amount the law excludes and any amount the recipient paid for it.
Employer-provided vehicle personal use: fair market value (lease cost of a comparable vehicle) or one of three special rules: cents-per-mile, commuting (commuting use only) and lease value.

facts.note: Pub. 15-B (2026) Commuting Rule p.27: each one-way commute valued at 1.50 per employee.

facts.value: Taxable noncash fringe benefits may be treated as paid per pay period, quarter, half-year, year or other basis, at least annually and all by 31 December; special accounting rule: benefits actually provided in November-December may be treated as paid in the next year. Not for transfers of investment-type personal property or real property (actual transfer date).

Add the value to regular wages for the payroll period and withhold on the total, or withhold at the 22% supplemental flat rate (37% on supplemental wages over 1 million); income tax, social security and Medicare are withheld on the date(s) the benefit is treated as paid.

facts.note: Pub. 15-B (2026) p.32: the employer may choose not to withhold income tax on personal use of an employer-provided highway motor vehicle, by written notice to the employee by 31 January or within 30 days after the vehicle is first provided, and must include the value in W-2 boxes 1, 3, 5 and 14; social security and Medicare are still withheld.

facts.value: Commuter highway vehicle and transit passes up to 350 a month and qualified parking up to 350 a month are excluded; not available to 2% S-corporation shareholders; cannot be offered through a cafeteria plan.
facts.note: TY2027 monthly limit 350 (Rev. Proc. 2026-35 / IR-2026-133); 2027 Pub. 15-B not yet published.
